The coffee chain plans to remodel as many as 9,000 of its company-operated North American stores as “community lounges,” adding seating, leather chairs, rugs, bookshelves, plants and artwork.

“We're not focused on changing major functional issues. We're really focused on creating a warmer and more welcoming experience for customers," said Dawn Clark, senior VP of coffee house design and concepts.
The investment is part of CEO Brian Niccol’s turnaround plan, which focuses on improving the in-store experience and service. Starbucks
is also targeting $2B in cost savings over the next two years.

is keeping the store upgrades relatively low-cost by retaining usable flooring and countertops. The renovations cost about $150,000 per store and can be completed overnight, avoiding temporary closures.
The strategy reverses some pandemic-era changes, when Starbucks
removed seating and increasingly focused stores on quick mobile-order pickups. Mobile orders now account for about one-third of U.S. transactions, more than twice their share in 2019.
